source.title: Count Pairs of Connectable Servers in a Weighted Tree Network

teaching.hint: In a tree, what can you infer when two paths leaving a server begin with the same edge?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Two paths from a center are edge-disjoint exactly when their endpoints lie in different incident branches.
solution_outline.approach: For each center, traverse each neighboring branch and count endpoints at divisible total distance. Combine each branch count with the sum of earlier branch counts, adding their product.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The running sum contains exactly qualifying endpoints in already processed branches; a new product counts pairs with one endpoint there and one in the new branch.
solution_outline.correctness: Tree paths are unique. Endpoints in one branch share its first edge, while different branches have disjoint paths. Traversal counts exactly the divisible-distance endpoints of each branch. Every qualifying unordered pair belongs to two distinct branches and is counted precisely when the later branch is processed.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n^2) time since each center visits all other nodes once; O(n) auxiliary space.
solution_outline.pitfall: Taking all pairs among qualifying endpoints also counts forbidden same-branch pairs.

common_wrong_turns: Taking all pairs among qualifying endpoints also counts forbidden same-branch pairs.
source_fidelity_notes: Made path length weighted and unordered-pair semantics explicit; retained exclusion of the center and edge-disjointness.
